pairs.question: Is it okay if I only smoke a little bit?
pairs.answer: There is no safe amount of smoking. The most important thing anyone can do to improve their health is to quit completely.
pairs.evidence: There is no safe amount of smoking. The most important thing anyone can do to improve their health is to quit completely.

pairs.question: What happens if I just cut back on smoking instead of quitting?
pairs.answer: Most people who cut back are not able to stay at a low level of use—they ultimately go back to using their usual amount. It's better to quit altogether.
pairs.evidence: Most people who cut back are not able to stay at a low level of use—they ultimately go back to using their usual amount.

pairs.question: How many times might I need to try to quit smoking?
pairs.answer: It may take a few tries, but you can stop using tobacco for good. Don't get discouraged!
pairs.evidence: It may take a few tries, but you can stop using tobacco for good.

pairs.question: What is the best thing I can do for my health regarding smoking?
pairs.answer: The best thing you can do for your health is to quit altogether. It's a tough journey, but worth it!
pairs.evidence: The best thing you can do for your health is to quit altogether.

pairs.question: What happens to my body soon after I quit smoking?
pairs.answer: Soon after you quit, your body will receive more oxygen and you will notice you have more energy and feel a little less stressed. It's a great step for your health!
pairs.evidence: Soon after you quit, your body will receive more oxygen and you will notice you have more energy and feel a little less stressed.

pairs.question: Will my cough go away if I quit smoking?
pairs.answer: Yes, your cough will go away, although for some it may take weeks as your lungs clean themselves by bringing up mucus. Hang in there; your body is healing!
pairs.evidence: Your cough will go away, although for some it may take weeks as your lungs clean themselves by bringing up mucus.

pairs.question: How does quitting smoking affect my senses?
pairs.answer: After quitting, your senses of taste and smell will improve. You'll likely enjoy food and scents much more!
pairs.evidence: Your senses of taste and smell will improve.

pairs.question: How does quitting smoking affect my risk of heart attack and stroke?
pairs.answer: Your risk of heart attack and stroke drop quickly after you quit smoking. That's a great reason to stick with it!
pairs.evidence: Your risk of heart attack and stroke drop quickly.

pairs.question: What are some benefits of quitting smoking besides health?
pairs.answer: You'll also have fewer wrinkles, whiter teeth, and will no longer smell like tobacco. Plus, you'll save money—lots of it!
pairs.evidence: You will also have fewer wrinkles, whiter teeth and will no longer smell like tobacco. You'll even save money—lots of it!

pairs.question: What can I do to boost my chances of quitting smoking?
pairs.answer: You can boost your odds by getting some help quitting. This means getting support from your friends and family, signing up for a program, and taking medication that can help you quit.
pairs.evidence: You can boost your odds by getting some help quitting, which means getting support from your friends and family, signing up for a program like and taking medication that can help you quit.

pairs.question: What medications can help me quit smoking?
pairs.answer: There are seven FDA-approved medications that can help you break your nicotine addiction. These include over-the-counter nicotine patches, lozenges, gum, and prescription nicotine nasal spray.
pairs.evidence: There are seven FDA-approved medications that can help you break your nicotine addiction. There are over-the-counter nicotine replacement therapies such as nicotine patches, lozenges and gum, and prescription nicotine replacement therapies and nicotine nasal spray.

pairs.question: Are there any non-nicotine medications I can take?
pairs.answer: Yes, there are two non-nicotine prescription drugs that can help you quit: bupropion (Zyban®) and varenicline (Chantix®).
pairs.evidence: There are also two non-nicotine prescription drugs that can help you quit: bupropion (Zyban®) and varenicline (Chantix®).

pairs.question: How should I use stop smoking medications?
pairs.answer: The most important thing to do is use the medication as directed. Most people do not use enough and do not use it long enough to obtain the best benefits.
pairs.evidence: The most important thing to do is use the medication as directed. Most people do not use enough and do not use it long enough to obtain the best benefits from stop smoking medications.

pairs.question: What should I do if my quitting strategies don't work?
pairs.answer: If your strategies don’t work, you will at least learn what not to do as you plan your next quit. Keep trying and learning from your experiences.
pairs.evidence: If not, you will at least learn what not to do as you plan your next quit. If you keep trying and keep learning from your experiences, you will be able to quit for good!

pairs.question: What challenges should I consider when quitting?
pairs.answer: Consider your biggest challenges from past attempts. Reflecting on these can help you think about what you could do differently this time.
pairs.evidence: What were your biggest challenges? What do you think you could do differently this time?

pairs.question: Are e-cigarettes safe or effective for quitting smoking?
pairs.answer: The FDA has not found any e-cigarettes to be safe or effective in helping people quit. It's best to talk to your healthcare provider about using one of the seven FDA-approved medications instead.
pairs.evidence: The FDA has not found any e-cigarettes to be safe or effective in helping people quit.

pairs.question: What does the American Lung Association say about e-cigarettes?
pairs.answer: The American Lung Association does not support the use of e-cigarettes. They encourage you to talk to your healthcare provider about proven methods to quit.
pairs.evidence: Based on this, the American Lung Association does not support the use of e-cigarettes.

pairs.question: Will I gain weight if I quit smoking?
pairs.answer: Some people do gain a few pounds when they quit. However, following a healthy eating plan and increasing physical activity can help you manage your weight.

pairs.question: Can I lose weight after quitting smoking?
pairs.answer: Yes, even if you gain some weight after quitting, you can lose it later. You'll still be healthier than when you were before.

pairs.question: What chemicals are in e-cigarettes?
pairs.answer: E-cigarettes can expose people to several chemicals known to have adverse health effects. It's important to be aware of these risks.

pairs.question: My friends still smoke, and it's tough for me to quit. What can I do?
pairs.answer: Quitting is a very personal decision, and while you can't make them quit, you can ask for their support. Tell them what you need to quit, like having tobacco-free zones around you.

pairs.question: What if I feel the urge to smoke? How long does it last?
pairs.answer: The urge will pass within three to five minutes, whether or not you use. Try to distract yourself during that time.

pairs.question: What can I do instead of smoking when I feel the urge?
pairs.answer: You can go for a walk around the block, call or text a friend, or drink a glass of water. These distractions can help you get through the moment.
